newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki tugged off highs by light profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki tugged off highs by light profit-taking.

text.p: Shares closed up but off session highs on Tuesday as investors booked profits following sharp gains on Monday and Tuesday morning, brokers said.
The HEX index rose 0.31 percent to 2,122.97. Volume was a healthy 352.06 million markka, 33 percent of it in Nokia.
Late afternoon news of SBC Warburg upgrading Nokia to a buy from sell cheered trade, and the telecom share closed 2.50 markka higher at 191.00, after trading down for most of the session.
State-owned chemicals group Kemira fell two markka to 47.00, discounting a new share issue and government offering, brokers said.
Kemira said it planned to seek permission to issue up to eight million new shares, while the government would lower its stake to 55 percent from 72.3 percent.
Steel-maker Rautaruukki rose one markka to touch a year-high 40.00 on brighter prospects for stainless steel prices, brokers said. Volume was fair for Rautaruukki at over 8 million markka.
Banking group Merita closed up 0.20 markka at 9.70, largely recovering from recent losses, brokers said.
"Market talk that Salomon Brothers has upgraded Merita has helped the share recover for the most part," one broker said.
